evidence.claim: Buhari was stepping down after the maximum eight years allowed by the constitution and had not named a successor.
evidence.title: Nigeria ruling party picks ex-governor of Lagos Tinubu to run for president
evidence.excerpt: Buhari was stepping down after the maximum eight years allowed by the constitution and had not named a successor.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting syndicated by Euronews; independent on succession facts, though secondhand on publication path.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly about Buhari’s end-of-term political position.
contrary_evidence: Syndicated copy, so the underlying Reuters text is stronger than the host page presentation.

evidence.claim: Buhari said Nigeria believes in the sanctity of constitutional term limits and had adhered to them, while preparing for elections and a successor to speak at the next UNGA.
evidence.title: Statement by President Buhari at the 77th Session of the United States General Assembly
evidence.excerpt: Buhari said Nigeria believes in the sanctity of constitutional term limits and had adhered to them, while preparing for elections and a successor to speak at the next UNGA.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary dated presidential speech with direct wording about term limits and transition.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is Buhari’s own statement about his transition posture and restraint.
contrary_evidence: A speech about term limits is not the same as an existential-risk policy action.

evidence.claim: CPJ said Nigerian authorities should release journalist Olamilekan Bashiru, who had been arbitrarily detained since May 13 after the DSS arrested him over a republished report about an Ogun state governor.
evidence.title: Nigerian journalist detained after republishing article about Ogun state governor
evidence.excerpt: CPJ said Nigerian authorities should release journalist Olamilekan Bashiru, who had been arbitrarily detained since May 13 after the DSS arrested him over a republished report about an Ogun state governor.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specialist press-freedom monitor with named officers, dates, and custody details, though reliant on reported allegations.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The arrest was carried out by federal security officers under Buhari's government, indicating a chilling effect attributable to the state.
contrary_evidence: CPJ is press-freedom focused and does not adjudicate the underlying governor allegations.

evidence.claim: CPJ said police arrested journalist Agba Jalingo on August 19 and moved him through multiple detention sites after a defamation and cyberattack complaint.
evidence.title: Nigerian journalist Agba Jalingo detained over defamation, cyberattack complaint
evidence.excerpt: CPJ said police arrested journalist Agba Jalingo on August 19 and moved him through multiple detention sites after a defamation and cyberattack complaint.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specialist press-freedom monitor with named arresting force and custody sequence, but still based on contemporaneous reporting.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The arrest and detention are attributable to state security organs within Buhari's domestic-security system.
contrary_evidence: The CPJ report is one case and does not establish the full national media environment by itself.

evidence.claim: Buhari said section 84(12) conflicted with the constitution and asked the National Assembly to amend the bill by deleting that section.
evidence.title: President Buhari’s Speech at the Signing of Electoral Bill 2022
evidence.excerpt: Buhari said section 84(12) conflicted with the constitution and asked the National Assembly to amend the bill by deleting that section.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential speech with explicit language about the requested amendment and legal rationale.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Buhari action; this shows an executive attempt to change the rules around political appointee participation.
contrary_evidence: He still assented to the broader reform package
the legislature later refused to follow his amendment request

evidence.claim: The Senate rejected President Buhari's executive request to amend the 2022 Electoral Act and refused to proceed while the matter was subject to a court order and due process concerns.
evidence.title: Senate rejects amendment to Electoral Act 2022
evidence.publisher: National Assembly of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
evidence.excerpt: The Senate rejected President Buhari's executive request to amend the 2022 Electoral Act and refused to proceed while the matter was subject to a court order and due process concerns.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official parliamentary record of the vote and the stated legal rationale.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but important as a constraint on Buhari's preferred rule change, not a presidential act itself.
contrary_evidence: The request itself came from Buhari
the legislature, not the president, stopped the amendment

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Buhari gave cabinet members a deadline to resign before seeking office, and ten ministers had already resigned to comply.
evidence.title: Four Nigerian ministers drop election bid to remain in cabinet
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Buhari gave cabinet members a deadline to resign before seeking office, and ten ministers had already resigned to comply.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting with direct, contemporaneous attribution and concrete cabinet compliance details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Buhari executive action through cabinet rules.
contrary_evidence: This also shows incumbents using state office while transitioning
four ministers initially stayed despite the deadline

evidence.claim: The ECOWAS Court ruled that Nigeria's Twitter ban was unlawful and said the Buhari administration must not repeat it.
evidence.title: Twitter ban in Nigeria unlawful, ECOWAS court rules
evidence.excerpt: The ECOWAS Court ruled that Nigeria's Twitter ban was unlawful and said the Buhari administration must not repeat it.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reputable local media report of a regional court ruling with a clear legal outcome and date.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct to the Buhari administration, though the ruling itself was issued by a regional court.
contrary_evidence: The case challenged a prior 2021 ban
this is a legal check after the fact rather than a presidential decision

evidence.claim: Buhari urged EFCC to avoid partisan politics and personal disputes and framed anti-corruption work as a transparency-and-accountability effort under the rule of law.
evidence.title: President Buhari Cautions EFCC on Political Interference, Commends Recovery of Looted Funds
evidence.excerpt: Buhari urged EFCC to avoid partisan politics and personal disputes and framed anti-corruption work as a transparency-and-accountability effort under the rule of law.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential speech with clear attributable language and dated publication.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Buhari speech; it reflects his stated integrity stance, not proof of practice.
contrary_evidence: The same year also saw criticisms of nepotism and censorship.
The source does not show how the EFCC message was implemented in practice.

evidence.claim: Buhari said departing ministers had served sacrificially, said cabinet selection aimed to produce the best and most competent, and thanked them for complying with his resignation directive.
evidence.title: President Buhari’s Speech at the Valedictory Session for Appointees Leaving the Cabinet to Pursue Political Ambition
evidence.excerpt: Buhari said departing ministers had served sacrificially, said cabinet selection aimed to produce the best and most competent, and thanked them for complying with his resignation directive.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential speech published the same day, with explicit language on appointments and resignation compliance.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and tied to the election-year cabinet resignations.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Buhari directive and public praise of compliance; high attribution.
contrary_evidence: The cabinet was still widely seen as patronage-heavy by critics.
The speech is self-described and does not independently verify competence or honesty.

evidence.claim: Buhari directed cabinet members seeking elective office to resign by May 16, 2022, to avoid benefiting from their government positions; the report says at least five cabinet members were seeking office.
evidence.title: Nigeria’s Buhari asks ministers with political ambition to resign
evidence.excerpt: Buhari directed cabinet members seeking elective office to resign by May 16, 2022, to avoid benefiting from their government positions; the report says at least five cabinet members were seeking office.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting is strong for the directive and resignations, though this is still a report of executive action rather than a legal record.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct presidential directive communicated through the information minister; attribution is strong.
contrary_evidence: The initial instruction did not clearly cover every political appointee outside the cabinet.
Emefiele was initially left in a gray zone, suggesting uneven enforcement.

evidence.claim: Buhari appointed the NNPC Limited board and management under the Petroleum Industry Act, naming members from multiple geopolitical zones and assigning executive roles.
evidence.title: President Buhari Appoints Board and Management of NNPC Limited
evidence.excerpt: Buhari appointed the NNPC Limited board and management under the Petroleum Industry Act, naming members from multiple geopolitical zones and assigning executive roles.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential appointment notice with full roster and legal basis.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct presidential appointment under Buhari’s authority.
contrary_evidence: The document itself does not prove competence or absence of patronage.
Later criticism of Buhari’s broader patronage patterns remains relevant.

evidence.claim: The article says Buhari approved Ahmed Halilu’s appointment as NSPMC managing director, identifies Halilu as Aisha Buhari’s brother, and argues this fit a broader pattern of family and close-relative appointments.
evidence.title: Buhari’s actions contradict nepotism comment
evidence.excerpt: The article says Buhari approved Ahmed Halilu’s appointment as NSPMC managing director, identifies Halilu as Aisha Buhari’s brother, and argues this fit a broader pattern of family and close-relative appointments.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Mainstream Nigerian business press with a dated, specific appointment claim and direct attribution.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct presidential approval of a family-linked appointment; attribution is strong for the appointment, weaker for the broader pattern unless corroborated elsewhere.
contrary_evidence: Halilu had relevant banking experience, which supporters used as a merit argument.
A family tie does not by itself prove self-enrichment, but it is strong evidence of favoritism risk.

evidence.claim: The ECOWAS Court held that the Buhari government’s Twitter suspension was unlawful and ordered Nigeria not to repeat it; the article links the ban to Twitter deleting Buhari’s tweet.
evidence.title: Nigeria’s Twitter ban is unlawful– ECOWAS Court
evidence.excerpt: The ECOWAS Court held that the Buhari government’s Twitter suspension was unlawful and ordered Nigeria not to repeat it; the article links the ban to Twitter deleting Buhari’s tweet.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent reporting on a court judgment with a clear legal outcome and identifiable causal context.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022, while addressing the government action that carried over into the year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong ruler attribution through the presidency and the reported trigger involving Buhari’s own tweet.
contrary_evidence: The government framed the suspension as a national-security response to fake news and subversion.
The court ruling does not itself prove Buhari personally authored every enforcement decision.

evidence.claim: A federal government statement said Buhari approved lifting the Twitter suspension effective 13 January 2022 after a committee recommendation.
evidence.title: FULL TEXT: FG Statement As Buhari Approves Lifting Of Suspension On Twitter Operations In Nigeria
evidence.excerpt: A federal government statement said Buhari approved lifting the Twitter suspension effective 13 January 2022 after a committee recommendation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: The published text reproduces the government statement and dates the approval and implementation clearly.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct presidential approval, though operationally carried out through NITDA and the ministerial committee.
contrary_evidence: The suspension had already lasted months and was widely criticized as censorship.
The government’s stated security rationale was rejected by the later ECOWAS ruling.

unresolved_gaps: Direct 2022 ruler-attributed existential-risk choice under Buhari's own authority
Independent corroboration of the HEU-to-LEU conversion and other nuclear-security claims
Independent evidence of actual conflict-management effect from Buhari's Ukraine/ECOWAS diplomacy
Direct documentary support for the contested Lake Chad weapons claim or any concrete cross-border security outcome
More precise chain-of-command and federal-versus-state attribution for abuses and remedies
More direct evidence on Buhari's personal role in media and protest restrictions, beyond security-service and state-level actions
Independent implementation evidence for the 2022 Electoral Act and related reforms
More household-level and distributional evidence on the effects of subsidy, naira redesign, and fiscal choices
Cleaner evidence on whether economic appointees were selected for competence versus loyalty
Independent outcome evaluation of school feeding, BHCPF, rotavirus rollout, and related social programs
Subnational delivery and attribution, especially for north-south and rural-urban differences
Direct evidence on assets, beneficial ownership, gifts, campaign finance, or family enrichment
More independent evidence on truthfulness, correction, and acceptance of scrutiny
Better separation of Buhari's personal conduct from broader authoritarian or state-level behavior
Audited completion data for major projects and service-delivery claims
Independent evidence that coordination bodies and new appointments changed implementation quality
